stories.title: Update: Jamia agrees to hold students' union polls after constitution is approved; one hunger striker served final notice
stories.body: The Tribune reported on Monday 26 October that Jamia Millia Islamia agreed to hold students' union elections 15 days after the union constitution is approved. It also said suspension and show-cause notices issued during the protests were revoked and a committee will examine the conduct of security personnel. Protesting students were to apologise publicly for statements against the administration, and the order asked that the protest be called off. PTI, republished by Vartha Bharati late that night, said the chief proctor issued a final notice dated 26 October asking one first-semester student still on hunger strike to leave the north campus, citing disciplinary and legal action. The student wanted a fixed deadline for approving the constitution.
stories.check: NEEDS CHECK: The Tribune does not confirm the hunger strike has ended; PTI says most protesters ended it but one continues, and The Federal (25 Oct) reported four still fasting. No deadline for approving the constitution was reported. The notice's claims are the university's; the student's response was not found. Confirm status with Jamia and the students.

stories.title: Update: Jamia cancels 106th Foundation Day and Talimi Mela 2026, due 29 October to 1 November
stories.body: Outlook India reported on Thursday 22 October that Jamia Millia Islamia cancelled its 106th Foundation Day celebrations and the Talimi Mela 2026, which had been scheduled from Thursday 29 October to Sunday 1 November. The report cites an internal communication dated 21 October from the Dean of Students' Welfare, which said normalcy had not been restored on campus and that protesting students had not accepted the university's proposed resolution. No new dates were reported. The cancellation was reported before the agreement described on Monday 26 October on union elections.
stories.check: Single source (Outlook India, 22 Oct). Confirm with Jamia whether the cancellation still stands after the 26 October agreement, and whether the Mela is rescheduled.

stories.title: Jamia's Foreign Languages department hosts Long Night of Literatures with EUNIC
stories.body: A Jamia Millia Islamia press release dated Monday 26 October says the Department of Foreign Languages held the University Edition of Long Night of Literatures 2026, with EUNIC, on Thursday 22 October at the FTK Auditorium, FTK-CIT Centre. Six writers from Slovenia, Italy, Germany, Portugal, Poland and Ukraine spoke on topics including AI and anthropology, Naples and Old Delhi, memory under political regimes, and the effects of war on children. The release says the dean of academic affairs welcomed guests and marked the university's 106th Foundation Day. The event ended with a photography session and refreshments.
stories.check: Single source: Jamia press release 6176. The release mentions marking the 106th Foundation Day at this event, while Outlook India (22 Oct) reported the Foundation Day celebrations cancelled; confirm with Jamia.
